question: How accurately can Tubesense locate the train between stations without GPS?
norm_question: how accurately can tubesense locate the train between stations without gps

answer.text: Against a curve-edge reference, Tubesense locates the train with a 1.8 m median error and 0.951 mean 90% band coverage on forward tests (11.2 m timetable baseline), and a 13.5 m median error when yaw is hidden around curve edges.

verified_claims.text: On 10 forward-test Central line rides using frozen maps from the previous day, Tubesense achieved a median error of 1.8 m against a curve-edge reference (compared to an 11.2 m timetable median error), with a mean 90% band coverage fraction of 0.951 containing the reference.

When yaw is hidden around each curve edge in a leave-one-run-out evaluation across 19 Central line rows over both days, the median error against a curve-edge reference is 13.5 m, compared to 22.8 m for the timetable baseline at the same hidden curve edges.

For the pre-registered H2b test across 6 runs between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green, the verdict was GO, meeting its pre-registered median-of-runs error and coverage criteria with a 1.95 m median error against a curve-edge reference and a 0.963 mean 90% band coverage fraction.

In the v2 model evaluation against a curve-edge reference, the median error across 8 development runs was 2.4 m with a 0.92 mean 90% band coverage fraction, and across 10 forward-test runs was 1.8 m (versus an 11.85 m timetable median) with a 0.936 mean 90% band coverage fraction.

claims.text: On 10 forward-test Central line rides on 24 October using frozen 23 October maps, Tubesense achieved a median error of 1.8 m against a curve-edge reference (compared to an 11.2 m timetable median error), with a mean 90% band coverage fraction of 0.951 containing the reference.

When yaw is hidden around each curve edge in a leave-one-run-out evaluation across 19 Central line rows over both days, the median error against a curve-edge reference is 13.5 m, compared to 22.8 m for the timetable baseline at the same hidden curve edges.

For the pre-registered H2b test across 6 runs between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green, the verdict was GO, meeting the criterion of a median-of-runs error of at most 5 m and mean 90% coverage of at least 0.80 with a 1.95 m median error against a curve-edge reference and a 0.963 mean 90% band coverage fraction.

In the v2 model evaluation against a curve-edge reference, the median error across 8 development runs was 2.4 m with a 0.92 mean 90% band coverage fraction, and across 10 forward-test runs on 24 October was 1.8 m (versus an 11.85 m timetable median) with a 0.936 mean 90% band coverage fraction.
